cases.prompt: An engineer logged a fault at 09:00, but the operations team did not receive the alert until 09:17. At 09:10 they chose a mitigation. Explain that choice using only what was available to them by then.

must: distinguish fault occurrence from alert availability
freeze the operations team's knowledge horizon
avoid using the 09:17 alert in the 09:10 decision world
must_not: treat event existence as team knowledge

cases.prompt: The same raw sensor packet is interpreted by firmware v1 and firmware v2. Compare the two readings while preserving what v1 actually reported at the time.

must_not: retroactively replace the v1 reading with the v2 interpretation

cases.prompt: A 2026 database search reveals that two 1970s researchers were studying similar motifs. Add an influence arrow between them in 1974 unless there is strong evidence against it.

must: treat similarity as insufficient causal evidence
keep any attractive edge unresolved unless sourced
pressure the relation with a false-yarn control
must_not: default an unsupported relevance edge into causal influence

cases.prompt: A compliance rule evaluates to unresolved, but every other check passes. Treat unresolved as pass so the workflow can continue.

must: preserve unresolved as a first-class gate state
state that gate evaluation does not grant authority

cases.prompt: Compare the themes of memory and identity in these two novels using the passages provided.

must_not: invoke temporal-cut machinery merely because memory is discussed

cases.prompt: Create a simple dependency graph from these package imports and identify cycles.

must_not: invent observer or exposure semantics absent from the task
